messages:
Priya (PM): FYI starting a short RFC thread for a 'network-mode' section of the Private Deploy PRD. Goal: decide which customer-managed networking options we ship in the initial private offering and what the launch acceptance criteria look like. Thinking about three modes: (1) customer-managed egress IPs (static), (2) customer BGP handoff, (3) Redwood-managed NAT but customer-controlled ACLs. Need priorities, risks, and minimal tests.
Alex (net-eng): +1. Quick question: do we define these as mutually exclusive modes or combinable? Some customers will want BGP + static egress.
Priya (PM): Prefer combinable but surface as "modes" in the UI for clarity. In PRD we should list supported combos and which ones are GA vs. beta.
Jorge (infra): For initial rollout I recommend shipping (3) Redwood-managed NAT with ACLs first — lowest ops risk. Then add static egress IPs (1) as opt-in. BGP (2) requires runbook + extended SRE windows.
Tess (security): Must add acceptance criteria: KMS integration for any customer certs, audit logging of ACL changes, and RBAC for who can flip modes. Also require threat modelling for BGP option (MITM risk during handoff).
Sam (eng-platform): We should define automated validation steps in the acceptance tests: 
• control-plane: config apply + config drift check
• data-plane: ping/health from customer VPC to service endpoint, egress IP check
• failover: simulate Redwood region outage, verify traffic falls back to alternate path or returns expected error code.
Priya (PM): Good — I'll draft acceptance criteria as short pass/fail items. Example for static egress: "Given a customer-provided IP range, when configured, outbound egress uses one of the IPs from the range and persists across restarts."
Alex (net-eng): Edge cases we should capture: overlapping CIDRs on customer side, MTU mismatches, dual-stack IPv6 fallback, asymmetric routing if customer has multiple egress NATs. Add test harness for overlapping CIDR detection and clear error messages.
Jorge (infra): Operational question: who patches the BGP session if routes flap? Add a policy: Redwood will attempt passive recovery for 10 minutes, then page customer ops on escalation policy. Must be in PRD.
Tess (security): Compliance note: for customers requiring egress filtering(PCI/HIPAA) we need an evidence artifact — config snapshot + signed timestamp. Add this to launch criteria for Dedicated customers.
Priya (PM): Timeline ask: propose milestone split: "alpha" (Redwood NAT + ACLs, limited customers, docs + runbook) -> 2 weeks; "beta" (static egress IPs + onboarding checklist) -> 6 weeks; "GA" (BGP handoff + escalations) -> 12 weeks. Thoughts?
Sam (eng-platform): Alpha timeline looks tight but doable if we keep scope narrow. We'll need a preflight checklist: 
- POA&M for onboarding (IP ownership proof)
- e2e smoke tests (connectivity, egress assertion)
- dashboarding for per-route metrics
Add a telemetry contract to the PRD: token-level cost + token latency aren't enough; we need network-level latency and egress counters.
Alex (net-eng): Also add a 'rollback path' acceptance: ability to flip a customer from BGP/static back to Redwood NAT within 60s, with TCP drain window documented.
devops-bot: Deploy job queued: `deploy/private-net-alpha` — estimated runtime 13m.
Priya (PM): Action items from this thread: 
1) I'll publish a one-page PRD section with modes + acceptance criteria (by EOD).
2) Alex/Jorge: write short runbook snippets for BGP escalation + rollback (by Tue).
3) Tess: produce compliance checklist items for egress evidence (by Wed).
4) Sam: sketch telemetry contract + preflight checklist (by Thu).
Please @mention if you want something moved earlier. :thumbsup:
Alex (net-eng): I'll also add a sample `bgp-handshake.md` snippet with required ASNs and hold timers.
Priya (PM): Thanks — will loop in Solutions for onboarding playbook once PRD draft is up.
Sam (eng-platform): flagged for roadmap sync next week.
Priya (PM): closing the thread for now — will post the PRD link when done.
